p.src: Now, while everyone was watching a performance of The Story of the Thorn Hairpin, Baoyu sat together with the young ladies. When Lin Daiyu saw that they had reached the scene entitled “The Husband's Offering,” she said to Baochai, “This Wang Shipeng really has no sense. He could have made his offering anywhere he pleased; why did he have to run all the way to the riverbank? As the saying goes, ‘The sight of a thing calls its owner to mind.’ All the waters under heaven flow from a common source. He had only to scoop up a bowlful of water anywhere, gaze at it, and weep his fill; that would have expressed all his feelings.” Baochai made no reply. Baoyu turned and called for some warmed wine with which to toast Xifeng.

p.src: It turned out that Grandmother Jia had declared that this day was no ordinary occasion and that Xifeng must be allowed to enjoy herself to the full. Grandmother Jia herself had not felt inclined to sit at the banquet. Instead, she reclined on a couch in the inner room and watched the play with Aunt Xue, choosing a few favorite dishes to set on a small table and eating and chatting at her leisure. She bestowed the food from her own two banquet tables on the maids, young and old, who had no tables of their own, as well as on the women in attendance, and told them all to sit beneath the veranda outside the windows, eat and drink as they pleased, and dispense with ceremony. Lady Wang and Lady Xing sat at a high table below, while the several tables outside were occupied by the young ladies. From time to time Grandmother Jia instructed Madam You and the others, “Seat Feng at the place of honor and entertain the guest of the day properly on my behalf. She works so hard all year long.” Madam You assented, but then replied with a smile, “She isn't used to the place of honor. Up there she doesn't know how to sit or where to put herself, and she refuses to drink as well.” Grandmother Jia laughed when she heard this. “You don't know how to manage her. Wait until I go and press her myself.” Xifeng hurried in and said with a smile, “Don't believe them, Old Ancestress. I've already had several cups.” Grandmother Jia laughed and ordered Madam You, “Quick, drag her back outside and pin her to her chair. All of you must take turns toasting her. If she still refuses to drink, I really shall go myself.” At this, Madam You laughingly pulled Xifeng outside again and seated her. She had a wine service brought and a cup filled, then said with a smile, “All year long you devote yourself so dutifully to the Old Lady, Her Ladyship, and me. I have nothing special with which to show you my affection today, so I have poured you a cup myself. Be a good girl and drink it from my hand.” Xifeng laughed. “If you sincerely mean to show me respect, kneel down and I'll drink it.” Madam You laughed. “Listen to you—you've quite forgotten who you are! Let me tell you, a chance like this comes only once in a great while. Once today is past, who knows whether you will ever again enjoy such treatment? Make the most of it and pour a couple of cups down your throat.” Unable to decline any longer, Xifeng drank two cups. The young ladies came next, and Xifeng had no choice but to take a sip from each one's cup. Seeing Grandmother Jia in such high spirits, Nanny Lai could hardly refrain from joining the fun. Leading several older serving women, she too came to offer a toast. Xifeng found it hard to refuse them as well and had to take another couple of sips. When Yuanyang and the others also came to toast her, Xifeng truly could drink no more and pleaded hurriedly, “Dear sisters, have mercy on me! Let me drink with you tomorrow instead.” Yuanyang laughed. “So you truly think we aren't worthy of the honor? Even when we offer a toast to Her Ladyship, she does us the honor of accepting it. Ordinarily you show us some consideration, yet today, in front of all these people, you suddenly put on the airs of a mistress. I should never have come. If you won't drink, we'll leave.” With that, she really did turn to go.

p.src: Xifeng could feel the wine weighing heavily on her; her heart was pounding as though it would leap into her throat. She wanted to go home and rest, but just then the acrobats came on. She therefore said to Madam You, “Have the reward money ready. I'm going to wash my face.” Madam You nodded. Waiting until no one was watching, Xifeng slipped away from the banquet and headed beneath the rear eaves of the rooms. Ping'er, who had been keeping an eye on her, hurried after her, and Xifeng leaned on her for support. They had only just reached the covered passage when they saw one of the young maids from Xifeng's rooms standing there. At the sight of the two women approaching, the girl turned and ran. Xifeng immediately grew suspicious and called out to her. At first the girl pretended not to hear. But when Ping'er too began calling after her, she had no choice but to come back. Xifeng's suspicions deepened. She hurried into the passage hall with Ping'er and ordered the young maid inside as well. After the lattice doors had been shut, Xifeng sat down on the steps of the little courtyard and ordered the girl to kneel. Then she barked at Ping'er, “Call two pages from the inner gate! Bring ropes and whips, and thrash this shameless little wretch who has no respect for her mistress until she's a bloody pulp!” The young maid was already frightened out of her wits. Weeping, she repeatedly knocked her head on the ground and begged for mercy. Xifeng demanded, “I'm not a ghost. When you saw me, why didn't you stand still and behave yourself? Why did you run away instead?” The young maid wept. “I really didn't see you coming, madam. I was worried because no one was watching the rooms, so I ran back.” Xifeng said, “If no one was in the rooms, who sent you here? Even if you didn't see me, Ping'er and I were behind you, straining our voices and calling you a dozen times, yet the more we called, the faster you ran. You weren't far away. Are you deaf? And still you dare talk back to me!” As she spoke, Xifeng raised her hand and slapped the girl across the face, knocking her sideways. She struck her once more on the other cheek, and at once both sides of the girl's face swelled up purple. Ping'er hastened to dissuade her. “Be careful, madam, or you'll hurt your hand.” Xifeng said, “You hit her now, and ask her why she ran. If she still won't tell us, tear her mouth to pieces!” The young maid continued to argue at first. But when she heard Xifeng threaten to heat a branding iron and sear her mouth, she finally wept and confessed, “The Second Master is at home. He sent me here to keep watch on you, madam, and told me that when I saw the banquet break up, I was to run back ahead of you and warn him. I never expected you to come back at this hour.” Xifeng sensed that there was more behind these words. “Why did he tell you to watch me? Could he be afraid that I might go home? There must be some other reason. Tell me at once, and from now on I shall treat you well. But if you don't tell me every detail, I shall have a knife brought this instant and slice the flesh from your body.”

p.src: As she spoke, she turned her head, pulled a hairpin from her hair, and jabbed wildly at the maid's mouth with it. Terrified, the girl dodged this way and that, pleading through her tears, “I'll tell you, madam, but please don't say you heard it from me.” Ping'er tried to calm her while urging the maid to speak quickly. The maid said, “Second Master only returned to his room a little while ago. After sleeping for a time, he woke and sent someone to see how you were getting on, madam. He was told that you had only just sat down at the banquet and would not be back for quite a while. Second Master then opened a chest and took out two pieces of silver, two hairpins, and two lengths of satin. He told me to deliver them secretly to Bao Er's wife and ask her to come in. She accepted the gifts and came straight to our rooms. Second Master ordered me to come and keep watch on you, madam. I don't know what happened after that.”

p.src: At this, Xifeng grew so furious that her whole body went limp. She hurriedly rose and made straight for home. Just as she reached the courtyard gate, she saw another young maid peering out from the doorway. The moment the girl caught sight of Xifeng, she ducked back and fled. Xifeng called her by name and ordered her to stop. The maid was quick-witted; seeing there was no escape, she came running out instead and said with a smile, “I was just on my way to tell you, madam. How fortunate that you've come.” “Tell me what?” asked Xifeng. The young maid told her what Second Master was doing at home, repeating everything the other girl had just said. Xifeng spat, “What were you doing earlier? Only now that I've caught you do you come pretending to be innocent!” With that, she raised her hand and struck the maid, sending her staggering, then crept softly up to the window. Listening there, she heard laughter and conversation inside. The woman laughed. “If only that hellcat of a wife of yours would hurry up and die.” Jia Lian said, “Even if she died, the next one I married would be just the same. What good would that do?” The woman replied, “When she dies, you could make Ping'er your proper wife. Surely that would be better.” Jia Lian said, “These days she won't even let me touch Ping'er. Ping'er too is full of grievances, but she dare not speak of them. Why was I fated to fall under the baleful star of such a she-demon?”

p.src: Hearing this, Xifeng shook violently with rage. When she heard them both praise Ping'er, she suspected that Ping'er too must have complained bitterly about her behind her back. The wine surged all the more fiercely within her, and without pausing to think, she turned and struck Ping'er twice, kicked the door open, rushed in, and, without allowing a word of explanation, seized Bao Er's wife and gave her a thorough beating. Afraid Jia Lian might escape, she planted herself in the doorway and cursed, “You filthy whore! You steal your mistress's husband and even plot to do his wife to death! Come here, Ping'er! You whores and cuckolds are all bound together, united in hating me, while outwardly you deceive me!” With that, she struck Ping'er several more times. Wronged yet unable to defend herself, Ping'er could only sob dry-eyed with fury and cry, “You are the ones doing these shameless things! Why drag me into it when I have done nothing?” Then she too seized Bao Er's wife and began to beat her. Jia Lian had drunk too much himself and, having come in in high spirits, had taken no care to keep the affair secret. The sight of Xifeng had already left him at a loss; now, seeing Ping'er join the fray, the wine inflamed his anger too. While Xifeng was beating Bao Er's wife, he had been both angry and ashamed, but could say nothing. Now that Ping'er was striking her too, he came forward, kicked at her, and cursed, “You filthy whore! How dare you raise your hand against her!” Timid before him, Ping'er hastily stopped and cried, “You were the ones talking behind my back. Why did you have to drag me into it?” Seeing that Ping'er was afraid of Jia Lian only enraged Xifeng further. She rushed forward and struck Ping'er again, insisting that she beat Bao Er's wife. Driven beyond endurance, Ping'er ran outside to find a knife and kill herself. The matrons and maids outside hurried to restrain and comfort her. Back inside, when Xifeng saw Ping'er run off to kill herself, she flung herself headfirst against Jia Lian's chest and cried, “You were all in league to harm me! Now that I have overheard you, you turn around and bully me instead. Go on, strangle me too!” In a fury, Jia Lian snatched a sword from the wall and said, “There's no need to go looking for death. I've had enough too. I'll kill you all together, pay with my life, and then we'll all be rid of this mess.” At the height of the uproar, Youshi and a group of others appeared. “What is the meaning of this?” they said. “Everything was fine a moment ago—how did such a quarrel break out?” At the sight of the others, Jia Lian played up his drunkenness all the more, putting on a show of authority and pretending in earnest that he meant to kill Xifeng. Now that others had arrived, Xifeng was no longer as fierce as before. Leaving everyone behind, she ran weeping toward Grandmother Jia's quarters.

p.src: By now the performance was over. Xifeng ran to Grandmother Jia, threw herself into her arms, and cried, “Ancestress, save me! Master Lian is trying to kill me!” Grandmother Jia, Lady Xing, Lady Wang, and the others hurriedly asked what had happened. Xifeng sobbed, “I had just gone home to change my clothes when, quite unexpectedly, I heard Master Lian talking to someone inside. I thought a guest had come and was too frightened to enter. I listened outside the window and discovered that he was plotting with Bao Er's wife. They said I was too formidable and planned to poison me to death, then make Ping'er his proper wife. Naturally I was angry, but I dared not quarrel with him, so I merely struck Ping'er twice and asked why she wanted to harm me. He was ashamed at being exposed and tried to kill me.” Grandmother Jia and the others believed every word and exclaimed, “This is outrageous! Bring that worthless wretch here at once!” Before she had finished speaking, Jia Lian came rushing after them with a sword in his hand and a crowd of people behind him. Jia Lian was openly relying on Grandmother Jia's habitual fondness for them, knowing that even his mother and aunt could do nothing to him; thus emboldened, he had come to make a scene. When Lady Xing and Lady Wang saw him, they angrily hurried to stop him and scolded, “You worthless wretch! You have become utterly lawless—the Old Lady is right here!” Jia Lian looked at them askance and said, “It is the Old Lady who has always indulged her. That is why she behaves this way and has even begun cursing me!” Furious, Lady Xing snatched the sword from him and repeatedly ordered him to “Get out at once!” But Jia Lian behaved like a spoiled fool and continued babbling shameless nonsense. Grandmother Jia said angrily, “I see that you hold none of us in any regard either. Send someone to fetch his father!” Only when Jia Lian heard this did he stagger away. Still in a sulk, he refused to go home and headed instead for the outer study.

p.src: Meanwhile, Lady Xing and Lady Wang also reproved Xifeng. Grandmother Jia laughed. “What does it matter? Young people are like greedy cats; how could they possibly refrain from such things? People have always come through youth in just this way. It is all my fault: he drank a little too much, and she became jealous as well.” At this, everyone laughed. Grandmother Jia continued, “Do not worry. Tomorrow I shall summon him and make him apologize to you. Do not go over there today and embarrass him.” Then she cursed again, “That little wretch Ping'er! I had always thought well of her. How could she be so wicked in secret?” Lady You and the others laughed. “Ping'er did nothing wrong. It was Xifeng who used the poor girl as an outlet for her anger. The husband and wife could not very well strike each other, so they both vented their fury on Ping'er. She has been wronged beyond measure, yet you are scolding her as well, Old Lady.” “So that is how it was,” said Grandmother Jia. “I thought that child did not seem like one of those bewitching, treacherous creatures. If so, poor thing, she has suffered their anger for no reason.” She called Amber over and said, “Go and tell Ping'er this from me: I know she has been wronged. Tomorrow I shall make Xifeng apologize to her. Today is her mistress's happy day, so she must not make a disturbance.”

Then she cursed again, “That little wretch Ping'er! I had always thought well of her. How could she be so wicked in secret?”
Lady You and the others laughed. “Ping'er did nothing wrong. It was Xifeng who used the poor girl as an outlet for her anger.
The husband and wife could not very well strike each other, so they both vented their fury on Ping'er.
She has been wronged beyond measure, yet you are scolding her as well, Old Lady.”
“So that is how it was,” said Grandmother Jia. “I thought that child did not seem like one of those bewitching, treacherous creatures.
If so, poor thing, she has suffered their anger for no reason.”
She called Amber over and said, “Go and tell Ping'er this from me: I know she has been wronged. Tomorrow I shall make Xifeng apologize to her.
Today is her mistress's happy day, so she must not make a disturbance.”

p.src: It turned out that Li Wan had already taken Ping'er into Prospect Garden. Ping'er was sobbing so hard that she could scarcely raise her head. Baochai consoled her. “You are a sensible person. You know how well Xifeng ordinarily treats you. Today she merely drank a little too much. If she did not vent her anger on you, could she have vented it on someone else? Then people would have laughed at her for being drunk. If you dwell only on your grievance now, would that not make all the kindness she has shown you in the past count for nothing?” As she was speaking, Amber arrived and relayed Grandmother Jia's message. Ping'er felt that her dignity had been restored, and only then did she gradually recover, though she did not return to the front apartments. After Baochai and the others had rested for a while, they went to see Grandmother Jia and Xifeng.

p.src: Baoyu invited Ping'er to come to Happy Red Court. Xiren hurried forward to receive her and said with a smile, “I had meant to invite you here from the start, but since the young mistress and the girls were all asking you to their rooms, I did not feel I could.” Ping'er smiled in return and thanked her. Then she added, “How could such a thing have started when all was well? For no reason at all, I had to endure that whole fit of anger.” Xiren said with a smile, “The Second Mistress usually treats you well. She merely lost her temper in the heat of the moment.” Ping'er replied, “I have no complaint against the Second Mistress. It was that wanton woman who brought this upon me, and she deliberately dragged me into it for sport; worse still, that muddleheaded master of ours turned around and struck me.” As she spoke, her sense of grievance welled up again, and she could not keep back her tears. Baoyu hastened to comfort her. “Dear sister, don't be sad. Let me apologize to you on behalf of both of them.” Ping'er smiled. “What has it to do with you?” Baoyu said with a smile, “We brothers and sisters are all one family. If they have wronged someone, it is only right that I should apologize on their behalf.” He went on, “What a pity your new clothes have been stained too. We have some clothes belonging to your sister Hua here. Why not change into those and spray yours with some heated wine before ironing them? You should redo your hair as well, and wash your face.” As he spoke, he ordered the little maids to draw water for her face and heat an iron. Ping'er had always heard people say that Baoyu knew especially well how to get along with girls. Baoyu, for his part, had kept his distance from her because she was Jia Lian's beloved concubine and Xifeng's confidante; and he had often regretted that he could never show her his full consideration. Seeing him behave so now, Ping'er silently reflected, “The stories are indeed true. He thinks of everything.” When she saw Xiren make a point of opening a chest and taking out two seldom-worn garments for her to change into, she quickly removed her own clothes and hurried away to wash her face. Baoyu stood nearby and smilingly urged her, “You should put on a little rouge and powder too, sister, or it will look as though you are sulking at Sister Xifeng. Besides, today is her special day, and the Old Lady has even sent someone to console you.” Ping'er saw the sense in this and went to look for powder, but could find none. Baoyu hurried to the dressing table, opened a porcelain box made in the Xuande kilns, and revealed a row of ten face-powder sticks shaped like tuberose stems. He picked one up and handed it to Ping'er. He said to her with a smile, “This isn't white lead. It is made from four-o'clock flower seeds, ground to powder and blended with perfume.” When Ping'er poured some into her palm and examined it, she found that it possessed all four virtues: it was light, white, rosy, and fragrant. It spread smoothly and evenly over the face and softened the skin, unlike other powders, which were bluish, heavy, rough, and apt to cake.

p.src: Next she noticed that the rouge did not come in the usual sheets. Instead, a paste resembling rose balm filled a tiny white-jade box. Baoyu said with a smile, “The rouge sold in the shops is never pure, and its color is weak too. This is made by pressing the juice from the finest rouge, filtering out all the sediment, mixing it with floral dew, and repeatedly steaming it. Just pick up a little with a fine hairpin and place it in your palm. Dissolve it with a drop of water and apply it to your lips; what remains in your palm will be enough for both cheeks.” Ping'er made herself up as instructed. The result was indeed extraordinarily vivid, and a sweet fragrance suffused her cheeks. Baoyu then used bamboo scissors to snip a twin-blossomed autumn orchid from the pot and placed it in her hair. Just then, a maid sent by Li Wan arrived to summon her, and only then did she hurry away.

p.src: Baoyu had always deeply regretted never having had the chance to show Ping'er his full consideration—for she was an exceptionally intelligent, refined, and handsome girl of the finest kind, quite unlike the common, clumsy fools of her sex. As it was Jinchuan'er's birthday, he had been unhappy all day. Yet unexpectedly, this disturbance had occurred later and given him the chance to show Ping'er a little kindness. It was an unlooked-for joy, one he had never imagined experiencing in this life. He reclined on the bed, inwardly content and pleased with himself. Then it suddenly occurred to him that Jia Lian cared only for gratifying his own lust and knew nothing of cherishing and nurturing a woman. He also thought how Ping'er had neither parents nor brothers nor sisters, and all alone had to attend upon both Jia Lian and his wife. In spite of Jia Lian's vulgarity and Xifeng's imperiousness, she managed everything tactfully and to perfection; yet today she had still suffered such cruelty. Her fate, he reflected, was even more wretched than Daiyu's. At this thought, sorrow rose in him again, and tears suddenly spilled from his eyes. Seeing that Xiren and the others were not in the room, he gave free rein to his grief and shed several bitter tears. Then he rose and saw that the wine sprayed on Ping'er's clothes had half dried. He ironed them and folded them neatly. Noticing that she had forgotten her handkerchief and that it was still stained with tears, he washed it in the basin and hung it up to dry. By turns glad and sorrowful, he remained melancholy for a while. Then he too went to Paddy-Sweet Cottage, where he chatted idly until the company dispersed after the lamps were lit.

p.src: Ping'er spent the night at Li Wan's quarters, while Xifeng remained with Grandmother Jia. When Jia Lian returned to his room that evening, he found it cold and deserted; too embarrassed to summon anyone, he could only pass the night as best he could. On waking the next day, he recalled what had happened and felt thoroughly ashamed, though regret came too late. Lady Xing, concerned that Jia Lian had been drunk the day before, hurried over early in the morning and summoned him to Grandmother Jia's apartments. Jia Lian had no choice but to swallow his shame, come before Grandmother Jia, and kneel down. “What is it?” Grandmother Jia asked him. Jia Lian hastily smiled ingratiatingly. “I had too much to drink yesterday and alarmed you, Old Ancestress. I have come today to receive my punishment.” Grandmother Jia spat in disgust. “You wretched creature! After swilling down that yellow brew, instead of lying quietly in your bed like a corpse, you took to beating your wife! Xifeng is forever boasting and ordinarily behaves like a tyrant, yet yesterday she was frightened into a pitiable state. If I had not been there and you had killed her, what would you be doing now?” Jia Lian felt full of grievances, but dared not defend himself and merely admitted that he was at fault. Grandmother Jia continued, “Are not Xifeng and Ping'er beauties themselves? Are they still not enough for you? Day after day you sneak about after women and drag every filthy, foul creature into your room. For the sake of such wanton women you beat your wife and even those who serve in your room. And you call yourself the son of a great house! You have brought disgrace upon your own claims. If you have any regard for me, get up. I shall forgive you, provided you behave yourself, apologize to your wife, and take her home. Then I shall be pleased. Otherwise, you may simply leave; I would not presume to accept your kneeling.” Hearing this, Jia Lian looked across at Xifeng. She wore no elaborate dress; her eyes were swollen from weeping, her face was unpowdered and sallow, and she seemed more pitiable and lovable than usual. He thought, “I may as well apologize. Then we can make peace, and I shall please the Old Ancestress too.” Having made up his mind, he smiled and said, “I dare not disobey the Old Ancestress, though this will only encourage her all the more.” “Nonsense!” Grandmother Jia laughed. I know that she has the best of manners and would never affront anyone. If she offends you in future, I shall naturally arbitrate then too and let you bring her to heel.”

p.src: At this Jia Lian scrambled to his feet, bowed with clasped hands to Xifeng, and said with a smile, “So it was all my fault. Second Mistress, please forgive me.” Everyone in the room burst out laughing. Grandmother Jia laughed. “Xifeng, you are not to be angry any longer. If you remain angry, I shall be angry with you.” She then ordered someone to fetch Ping'er and instructed Xifeng and Jia Lian to console her. The sight of Ping'er made Jia Lian even less mindful of appearances—for, as the saying goes, “A wife is not so enticing as a concubine, nor a concubine as a stolen tryst.” Prompted by Grandmother Jia's words, he hurried forward and said, “You were wronged yesterday, my dear, and it was all my fault. Your mistress wronged you because of me as well. Besides apologizing for myself, I shall apologize on your mistress's behalf too.” With that he bowed to her with clasped hands, making Grandmother Jia laugh; even Xifeng smiled. Grandmother Jia then told Xifeng to console Ping'er. Ping'er hastened forward and kowtowed to Xifeng. “On your birthday of all days, Mistress, I angered you. I deserve to die.” Xifeng already regretted that, having drunk too much the day before, she had forgotten their longstanding affection, lost her temper, and humiliated Ping'er without cause merely because she had listened to someone else's words. Now, seeing Ping'er behave in this way, she felt both ashamed and heartsore. She hastily pulled her up, and tears fell from her eyes. Ping'er said, “I have served you for all these years, Mistress, and you have never so much as touched me with one fingernail. Even though you struck me yesterday, I bear you no resentment. It was all that wanton woman's doing, so no one can blame you for being angry.” As she spoke, tears fell from her eyes too. Grandmother Jia ordered that the three of them be escorted back to their rooms. “If any one of you mentions this affair again, report it to me at once. I do not care who it is—I shall give that person a beating with my walking stick.”

p.src: The three of them once more kowtowed to Grandmother Jia and to Ladies Xing and Wang. An old nurse acknowledged the order and escorted the three of them back. Once they reached their room and Xifeng saw that no one else was present, she said, “Am I some King of Hell, or some hideous demon? That wanton woman cursed me to die, and you joined her in cursing me. Even if I am unkind for a thousand days, surely there is one day when I am kind. How pitiful I am! After enduring so much, I find myself worth less than a wanton woman. How can I have the face to go on living like this?” With that, she began to weep again. Jia Lian said, “Are you still not satisfied? Think carefully: who was more at fault yesterday? Today, before everyone, it was I who knelt down and apologized. You have had more than enough vindication. Yet you are still going on about it. Must I kneel to you here before you will stop? It does no good to insist on having the upper hand in everything.” His words left Xifeng without an answer, while Ping'er gave a little snort of laughter. Jia Lian laughed too. “There, all is well again! Truly, I do not know what to do with either of you.”

p.src: As they were speaking, a servant woman came in and reported, “Bao Er’s wife has hanged herself.” Jia Lian and Xifeng were both startled. Xifeng quickly concealed her fear and instead snapped, “So she’s dead! What is there to make such a fuss about?” Presently, Lin Zhixiao’s wife came in and quietly told Xifeng, “Bao Er’s wife has hanged herself, and her relatives on her mother’s side mean to bring a lawsuit.” Xifeng laughed. “That suits me perfectly. I’ve been longing for a lawsuit!” Lin Zhixiao’s wife said, “I have just had everyone reason with them. We frightened them a little too, and promised them some money, so they have agreed to let the matter rest.” “I haven’t a single coin!” said Xifeng. “Even if I had money, I would give them none. Let them sue if they please. “You are not to dissuade them or intimidate them either. Just let them go ahead and sue. “And when their case fails, I shall charge them with using a corpse to extort money!” Lin Zhixiao’s wife was at a loss, but when she saw Jia Lian signal to her with his eyes, she understood and went outside to wait. Jia Lian said, “I’ll go out and see how matters stand.” “You are not to give them any money,” said Xifeng. Jia Lian went straight out and conferred with Lin Zhixiao. He sent men to use both persuasion and pressure, and the matter was finally settled with a promise of two hundred taels for the funeral expenses. Fearing some further trouble, Jia Lian also sent word to Wang Ziteng and had several constables and coroners summoned to assist with the funeral arrangements. Seeing such a show of authority, her relatives dared not argue further even if they wished to; they could only swallow their anger and remain silent. Jia Lian then ordered Lin Zhixiao to enter the two hundred taels in the annual household accounts, spreading the sum among various expenses to cover it. He also privately gave Bao Er some silver and consoled him, saying, “Another day I shall choose a good wife for you.” Bao Er had gained both consideration and money, so why would he refuse? He therefore continued to ingratiate himself with Jia Lian, but that need not detain us.
